mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the chromosome copies before splitting the cell was worthwhile: the planned intermediate inset and two nuclei distinguish chromosome separation from division of the cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: Growth was the least engaging passage: its materials and result were clear, but the only available action made the progression predictable.

surprise.text: The replication illustration distinguishes old from newly synthesized strands and explicitly leaves out RNA and protein-production arrows, reinforcing that copying DNA is a separate process.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although every step had only one offered combination. The spindle and actin–myosin ring were named without much explanation of how their components work.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the daughter cells take different paths, though the forced sequence offered few meaningful decisions in this chapter.
